subject: FastStart streaming requirements & ops playbook (post-call)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@finnect.com>, Finnect Platform Team <ops@finnect.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: FastStart streaming requirements & ops playbook (post-call)

Thanks again for your time this morning — really helpful to walk through your FastStart integration goals. Below is a concise recap of the performance targets and the immediate information we need to validate a pilot and propose an SLA for production. I pasted the answers we captured live and added action items.

Summary of call notes (what we heard)
- Primary objective: smooth user experience for live quote/chat flows in the mobile app and web console.
- Expected peak concurrent users during market hours: ~1,200 (concurrent sessions), average concurrent during steady-state: ~240.
- Typical request profile: 1–3 prompts per session, median request length ~40 tokens (prompt) + ~150 tokens (response).

Requested TTFT & streaming constraints (proposed)
- Target median time-to-first-token (TTFT): <= 150 ms for US region (p50).
- Target p95 TTFT: <= 350 ms.
- Target p99 TTFT (SLA-affecting): <= 600 ms — required for contractual SLA discussion.
- Throughput baseline: 200 QPS sustained throughput across a dedicated pool; burst capacity to 350 QPS for market opens.
- Concurrency: design for 1,500 concurrent streams with automatic routing to dedicated nodes.
- Streaming mode: WebSocket preferred for mobile clients; SSE acceptable for web fallback but note SSE reconnect behavior on intermittent mobile networks.
- Chunk cadence suggestion: aim for 200–300 ms per chunk for streaming responses that are >200 tokens; 100–150 ms for short responses to keep perceived latency low.

Open items we need from Finnect (action by your team)
1) Please share a 48-hour sample of production traffic (start/end timestamps, per-request tokens in/out, client type) — file template attached (Finnect-SLO-request.csv).
2) Confirm acceptable p99 TTFT for negotiations (you mentioned 500 ms as a preference; we used 600 ms above as a conservative SLA floor).
3) Clarify mobile OS mix (iOS/Android split) and whether WebView clients are in scope.

What we will deliver next (RACI & timing)
- By EOD Tue (2027-05-24): engineering will produce a pilot capacity/latency plan and a preliminary cost estimate for Dedicated pool sizing (owner: Karthik).
- By Thu (2027-05-27): we can schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive to validate chunk cadence, codec choices, and fallback behavior (owner: Alex).
- Preflight: we attached a short runbook (faststart-preflight-runbook.pdf) with steps for test credentials, ingest endpoints, and a small test harness you can run locally.

Immediate ask / Next step
- Sara — can you confirm you can provide the traffic sample by Tue 05/24 and whether Finnect is comfortable with WebSocket as the primary streaming transport? If WebSocket is blocked by security policy, note that SSE is doable but we'll plan for more aggressive client-side reconnects and smaller chunk sizes.

Attachments: Finnect-SLO-request.csv (template), faststart-preflight-runbook.pdf, call-recording-20270522.mp4 (link stub).

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147
https://redwood.com
From: Sara Patel <sara@finnect.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Finnect Platform Team <ops@finnect.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FastStart streaming requirements & ops playbook (post-call)

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Traffic sample: ops can export the 48-hour slice but it'll need to be scrubbed first; aim for delivering by EOD Wed 05/25. We can provide anonymized session IDs, timestamps, token counts, and client type.
2) TTFT targets: our internal Product lead prefers p99 <= 500 ms; if you can hit that with Dedicated we have a stronger case for procurement.
3) Mobile: currently 60% iOS / 35% Android / 5% WebView. WebView is flaky on older Android devices, which is why SSE fallback would be useful.
4) Fallback behavior: if WebSocket drops we would like a deterministic retry window (2s, 5s, 10s) and to fall back to polling only if reconnect fails after X attempts. Can you confirm Redwood has a recommended retry strategy we can adopt?

Procurement timeline: we are on a tight calendar — decision maker review by Jun 9. Having a p99 <= 500 ms commitment for the pilot will materially increase the likelihood of signing a pilot contract.

I'll attach the scrubbed export when ops finishes. Let me know if you need a short call with our mobile engs.

—
Sara Patel
Head of Product, Finnect
sara@finnect.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FastStart streaming requirements & ops playbook (post-call)

Adding the engineering perspective — quick notes and assumptions based on what was discussed. Quoting Sara where helpful: 

> TTFT targets: p99 <= 500 ms preferred (Sara)

Assumptions
- US region only for pilot; colocated edge nodes near us-east-1 recommended.
- Model family: customer signaled intent to use a mid-sized instruction-following model (~7B params) with fp16/4-bit quantization for cost. Exact model unknown — we should ask Finnect to confirm model affinity.

Technical notes / recommendations
- Achievability: p50=150ms / p95=350ms / p99<=500ms is achievable with a Dedicated pool sized to their concurrency patterns and with aggressive KV-prefix caching for repeated prompt prefixes.
- Batching: keep batch windows <20 ms for low single-request latency. Continuous batching with micro-batches works well if we reserve dedicated capacity.
- Streaming transport: WebSocket has the lowest friction for mobile; SSE fine for desktop. On flaky networks (mobile), reduce chunk size to 80–120 tokens and pace at ~200 ms to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Fallback policy: recommend client-side reconnect plan: immediate attempt, t=2s, t=5s, t=10s, then switch to polling for up to 30s before full abort. We'll provide a JS/Android sample in the deep-dive.

Questions for product/solutions
- Do we commit to a contractual p99 number for the pilot or only a best-effort target? (Marissa to confirm with Finnect).
- Need Finnect to indicate any throughput spikes (eg daily market open) that would require burst capacity.

I'll prepare a short pilot sizing doc and a minimal test harness (wrk-based) so Finnect can replay traffic to our test endpoints. Planning to deliver that by Tue 05/24.

—
Karthik Iyer
Principal Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@finnect.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T17:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FastStart streaming requirements & ops playbook (post-call)

Great — thanks Sara and Karthik. Quick confirmation of next steps so procurement has a clear timeline: 

- Finnect: deliver scrubbed 48-hour traffic slice by EOD Wed 05/25 (Sara / ops).
- Redwood Eng (Karthik): pilot sizing doc + test harness by Tue 05/24.
- Redwood Solutions (Alex): schedule 60-minute technical deep-dive for Thu 05/27 (Alex to send calendar invite).
- Contracting: Marissa to submit a pilot commercial term sheet (target draft by Fri 05/28) for their procurement review.

Note on the p99 ask: we'll treat p99 <= 500 ms as the aspirational SLA trigger for procurement conversations; for the contract we will map the SLA windows to Dedicated sizing and include fallback policies for network variance. We will not include punitive financial credits on the initial pilot; if Finnect moves to a production commit, we can discuss an SLA-backed clause.

Sara — I'll follow up with a short invite for a mobile eng sync before the deep-dive so we can flush out the WebView/SSE corner cases. Also attaching the runbook and the SLO CSV template again for reference.

Thanks everyone — see calendar invite from Alex shortly.

—
